generic_sampling_rules.text_columns: Sample from a per-column pool built from observed distinct values plus fresh synthetic values; 20-50% of rows reuse an existing value (duplicates for DISTINCT), the rest are fresh. For each LIKE/equality literal in per_column_exceptions, force-include the literal, one near-variant (one char substituted/appended, or case-flipped), and a prefix/suffix extension in the pool so each appears at least once per instance.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_columns: Sample integers uniformly within the column range; for boundary targets include each listed literal and one step on each side (step = 1 unless stated).
generic_sampling_rules.nullable_columns: Each nullable column gets NULL in a share of rows matching the compact database share (5-30% for COUNT columns, 0% for NOT NULL); at least one NULL row per nullable column per instance. NULL is a value: planted NULLs are never replaced to satisfy a rule.
generic_sampling_rules.join_columns: For FK columns, generate parent rows first; assign child FK values from parent keys, plus a share of child rows with NULL FK (where nullable) and a share of parent rows with no children.
generic_sampling_rules.order_tie_columns: For ORDER/LIMIT columns, plant ties on the actual aggregate (COUNT(*) and COUNT(tags.tag)) at the listed ranks by controlling the number of tags per torrents group so that two groups share the same COUNT at rank 1 and rank ~100.

semantic_rules_and_formulas.formula: groupYear IS NULL OR groupYear BETWEEN -1562 AND 2015
releaseType IS NULL OR releaseType IN ('single','album','live album','ep','unknown','soundtrack','concert recording','anthology')

supporting_evidence.torrents.id: Sample rows id 0..7 all non-null, primary key.
supporting_evidence.torrents.groupYear: Sample groupYear 1979..1986 within range; boundary targets from stats distinct=38.
supporting_evidence.torrents.releaseType: Sample releaseType values single, album, live album, ep, unknown, soundtrack, concert recording, anthology (8 of 15 distinct).

generation_specification.uncertainty: releaseType enum lists only the 8 observed values of 15 distinct; remaining 7 values unknown. groupYear range upper bound 2015 inferred from boundary targets, not from sample. tags.id is a nullable FK to torrents.id (NULL allowed, non-NULL values drawn from torrents.id); the tags.id -> torrents.groupId join seen in the atomic summary is a query-level join pattern, not a schema FK, and is not listed under dependencies. Tie planting targets the aggregate COUNT(*) / COUNT(tags.tag) at ranks 1 and ~100.

issues.title: Generated instances do not preserve the compact (D_c) rows
issues.evidence: Execution feedback: every one of the 20 instances reports 'compact_rows_missing' (dc_rows_missing_or_changed = 215 per instance; constraint_violations.dc_rows_missing_or_changed lists torrents 2280 rows / tags 2020 rows across 20 instances). The writer is invoked as write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p) in cli.py:_one with no orig_path argument, so writer.py takes the `fresh = True` branch and only executes schema.ddl — it never copies the original database. The generated rows are then inserted into an empty schema, so the compact rows are absent. This is why 'rows_added' is negative in 19/20 instances (the checker compares against the compact baseline) and why validity is 0/20.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original database path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. add orig_path to the args dict in cli.py and call write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p, orig_path=a['orig'])), so the compact database is copied first and generated rows are appended on top of it. Re-run and confirm dc_rows_missing_or_changed == 0 and rows_added > 0 for all instances.

issues.title: Writer inserts each accepted row twice (execute + re-batch) and counts are inconsistent
issues.evidence: writer.py: for each row it calls con.execute(sql, r) inside the loop and appends to `good`, then sets ok[t] = len(good) with the comment 'batch the accepted rows too (idempotent no-op if already inserted)'. There is no second executemany, so the comment is misleading, but more importantly the per-row execute means PK/UNIQUE collisions are silently swallowed into `bad` while `ok` counts only successes — combined with the missing compact copy this produces the negative rows_added figures. The reported rows_added (torrents 1628, tags 1471) also does not match the per-instance checker output (negative deltas), indicating the writer's accounting is not aligned with what actually lands in the file.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the dead 'batch' comment and either use executemany for accepted rows or keep per-row execute but make ok/bad accounting reflect actual inserted rows. After fixing the compact-copy issue, verify rows_added reported by the program equals the checker's positive delta.

issues.title: FK dependency tags.id -> torrents.groupId is not a real foreign key and conflicts with the schema
issues.evidence: The supplied schema declares only `tags.id references torrents` (i.e. tags.id -> torrents.id). The atomic summary and the specification's `dependencies` list add a second dependency tags.id -> torrents.groupId, and the spec's uncertainty note admits 'FK tags.id references both torrents.id and torrents.groupId per atomic summary; treated as two dependencies.' The program's fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws tags.id from _parent_values for whichever parent the schema.fks dict holds; read_schema builds fks from pragma foreign_key_list, which will only yield tags.id -> torrents.id. So the groupId dependency is never actually enforced, and the spec's claim is unsupported by the DDL.
issues.requested_revision: Either drop the tags.id -> torrents.groupId dependency from the specification (it is not in the DDL and cannot be enforced), or, if the atomic summary genuinely reflects a query pattern, record it as a query-level join pattern rather than a schema FK. Do not list it under `dependencies` as a copied-column FK.

issues.title: releaseType enum is under-specified and the program does not enforce it
issues.evidence: semantic_rules_and_formulas states releaseType IN ('single','album','live album','ep','unknown','soundtrack','concert recording','anthology'), but the spec's own uncertainty says only 8 of 15 distinct values are known. The program's StringSampler for releaseType uses boundary values from like_near_variant/comparison_boundary plus observed values and fresh perturbations (values.py StringSampler.sample appends random chars, drops chars, etc.), so generated releaseType values will frequently fall outside the declared enum. No CHECK constraint exists in the DDL, so this is not an integrity failure, but it violates the stated semantic rule.
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) restrict releaseType sampling to the declared enum (add an enum sampler or pass the enum as the only allowed pool), or (b) remove the IN(...) formula from semantic_rules_and_formulas and document releaseType as free text. Pick one and make spec and program agree.

issues.title: groupYear range upper bound 2015 is asserted but not enforced; boundary values outside range are generated
issues.evidence: semantic_rules_and_formulas: groupYear IS NULL OR groupYear BETWEEN -1562 AND 2015. But per_column_exceptions for groupYear list boundary values including -1563 and 2001, and column_bounds (schema.py) computes lo = min(allv)-2, hi = max(allv)+2, so the NumberSampler for groupYear is given lo/hi spanning roughly -1565..2003 — fine — but the spec's own boundary list includes -1563 which is below the declared lower bound -1562. The program will therefore emit groupYear = -1563, violating the stated formula. There is no CHECK constraint, so integrity passes, but the semantic rule is contradicted by the spec's own boundary targets.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the boundary list with the formula: either widen the formula to include -1563 (and any other listed boundary) or drop -1563 from the boundary targets. Also confirm the 2015 upper bound is intended (spec uncertainty admits it is inferred, not observed).

issues.title: tags.id NULL share is generated but tags.id is the FK to torrents.id; NULL FK rows are allowed by the interface but the spec's null_targets and the DDL disagree
issues.evidence: nullable_columns feedback: 'tags.id: generated rows: NULL 10 / 167'. The DDL declares tags.id as `constraint tags_torrents_id_fk references torrents` with no NOT NULL, so NULL is permitted. The spec lists tags.id under null_targets and under null_in_count_column with 5-30%. The program's fill_foreign_keys_consistently gives child_null_share=0.15 default and _apply_null_rule also applies. This is consistent with the interface's NULL rule, but note the spec's `dependencies` treats tags.id as a copied FK column while also allowing NULLs — the two are compatible only because the interface says NULL is a value. No change strictly required, but the spec should state explicitly that tags.id is a nullable FK so the dependency and NULL rules are not read as contradictory.
issues.requested_revision: Add an explicit note in the specification that tags.id is a nullable FK (NULL allowed, non-NULL values drawn from torrents.id), so the dependency entry and the null_in_count_column entry are not in tension.

issues.title: Tie planting for ORDER/LIMIT is a no-op in practice
issues.evidence: instance.py _plan_ties returns {'tie_size': sizes[table]//3 + 1} and _plant_ties only acts if n >= 2*tie + 2, i.e. n >= 2*(n//3+1)+2, which for n=200 gives tie=67 and requires n>=136 — satisfied — but it overwrites artist values in ranges [tie,2*tie) and [3*tie,4*tie) with vals[0] and vals[2*tie]. This plants ties on the artist column, not on the aggregate COUNT(*) / COUNT(tags.tag) that the spec's ties_for_order_limit targets. The spec asks for ties at rank 1 and rank ~100 on COUNT(*) and COUNT(tags.tag); the program ties artist values, which only indirectly affects group counts and does not guarantee the requested tie ranks. Construction feedback shows construction_pairs separated 19/85 with no per-group breakdown, so tie behavior is unverified.
issues.requested_revision: Either implement tie planting on the actual aggregate (e.g. by controlling the number of tags per torrents group so that two groups share the same COUNT at rank 1 and rank ~100), or remove the ties_for_order_limit exception from the spec if it cannot be honored. Document which aggregate is tied.

issues.title: Unresolved: construction separation is low (19/85) and no per-group evidence is provided
issues.evidence: construction_pairs: eligible 85, separated 19, unknown_executions 0, construction_pairs_by_group empty. The instructions note a missing separation alone does not prove a generation error, but with 66/85 pairs unseparated and no per-group breakdown, it is not possible to confirm that the intended value variation (like/near variants, boundary values, duplicate shares) actually distinguishes the target queries. The nullable_columns feedback shows NULLs are generated for all nullable columns, which is good, but the like_near_variant and comparison_boundary targets are only sampled with probability 0.15 in StringSampler.sample (boundary branch) and via variants_of with 0.2 probability, so many instances may lack the specific near-variants.
issues.requested_revision: Provide per-group construction feedback (construction_pairs_by_group) and, if separation remains low, increase the probability/guarantee that each like_near_variant literal and its variants appear at least once per instance (e.g. force-include the literal and one variant in the sampler's element pool rather than relying on random draws).

unresolved_checks: Whether the compact database is actually present in the generated files (the writer never copies it; the checker reports 215 missing/changed compact rows per instance).
Whether the tags.id -> torrents.groupId dependency is intended as a schema FK or only a query join pattern.
Whether releaseType is meant to be a closed enum or free text.
Whether groupYear boundary -1563 is intended to be inside the allowed range.

Per-group construction separation evidence is absent (construction_pairs_by_group empty).

issues.evidence: Specification's semantic_rules_and_formulas constrain torrents.releaseType to a fixed enum of 8 values ('single','album','live album','ep','unknown','soundtrack','concert recording','anthology'), but the uncertainty note admits only 8 of 15 distinct observed values are known. The program (values.py StringSampler) does not enforce this enum at all; it samples from observed values plus perturbations, so generated releaseType values will include near-variants like 'singlf', 'albun', 'ALBUM' that violate the stated enum. Execution feedback shows no integrity failures because the enum is not a DB constraint, so this is a spec-vs-program mismatch rather than a constraint violation.
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) drop the releaseType enum formula from semantic_rules_and_formulas (it is not a real DB constraint and conflicts with the like_near_variant/comparison_boundary targets that deliberately plant 'singlf','albun','ALBUM', etc.), or (b) explicitly state that the enum is a soft/observed domain and that near-variants are intentional exceptions. Do not add a hard enum check to the program, since it would suppress the required near-variant targets.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_plan_ties` returns only `{'tie_size': sizes[table]//3 + 1}` and `_plant_ties` copies the first artist value into rows [tie, 2*tie) and a second value into [3*tie, 4*tie). This plants ties on the artist column, not on the aggregate COUNT(*)/COUNT(tags.tag) at ranks 1 and ~100 as the spec's ties_for_order_limit target requires ('tie_on': ['COUNT(*)','COUNT(tags.tag)'], 'tie_at_rank': [1,100]). The spec's generic_sampling_rules order_tie_columns explicitly says ties must be planted 'by controlling the number of tags per torrents group so that two groups share the same COUNT at rank 1 and rank ~100'. The current implementation does not control tag counts per torrent group at all.
issues.requested_revision: Implement tie planting on the aggregate: after generating tags, adjust the number of tags per torrents group so that at least two groups share the same COUNT at rank 1 and at least two groups share the same COUNT at rank ~100 (for both COUNT(*) and COUNT(tags.tag)). Alternatively, if aggregate-level tie planting is out of scope, remove the ties_for_order_limit exception for torrents.artist from the spec so the program and spec agree.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_parent_values` returns `gen if gen else compact`, i.e. it uses only generated parent keys when any exist, ignoring compact parent keys. The spec's dependencies and the unmatched_join_rows targets require child FK values to be drawn from parent keys including compact rows (so that joins against the compact DB still match). With this logic, tags.id values are drawn only from generated torrents.id values, so a join tags.id = torrents.id will never match compact torrents rows. Execution feedback shows 0 FK violations only because foreign_keys=OFF in writer.py and tags.id is not a declared FK in the schema; the semantic dependency is still violated.
issues.requested_revision: Change `_parent_values` to return the union of compact and generated parent keys (e.g. `compact + gen`), so child FK values can match both compact and generated parent rows, consistent with the spec's dependency and unmatched_join_rows targets.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_spec_kw` only sets `lo`/`hi` for integer columns when the column type string contains 'int'. For torrents.groupYear (INTEGER) this works, but the boundary targets for groupYear include -1562 and 2015; column_bounds computes lo=min-2, hi=max+2, so the sampler range is [-1564, 2017], which is fine. However, the spec's semantic rule 'groupYear IS NULL OR groupYear BETWEEN -1562 AND 2015' is not enforced by the program: NumberSampler draws uniformly in [lo,hi] and can produce values outside [-1562,2015] (e.g. -1564, 2016, 2017). Execution feedback shows no not_null violations because the rule is not a DB constraint, but the spec formula is violated.
issues.requested_revision: Either tighten column_bounds for groupYear to exactly [-1562, 2015] (no ±2 padding) so the sampler cannot exceed the stated range, or relax the spec formula to match the padded range. The current ±2 padding in column_bounds is inconsistent with the stated BETWEEN -1562 AND 2015 rule.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_apply_null_rule` is called with `(t,)` as the `tables` argument but the function signature is `_apply_null_rule(tm, cols, null_shares, tables, rng)` and the body never uses `tables`. More importantly, `_apply_null_rule` runs after `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` and after `sample_fresh_primary_keys`/`drop_unique_duplicates`, so it can overwrite FK values (including tags.id) with NULL after FK consistency was established, and it can overwrite PK values with NULL if a PK column is nullable in the schema (torrents.id is NOT NULL per spec, so this is safe there, but tags.id is nullable and is a PK in the schema — `_apply_null_rule` skips `cm.pk_pos > 0`, so tags.id is not nulled by this path; however `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` already nulls tags.id at child_null_share=0.15, which is within the 5-30% window). The execution feedback shows tags.id NULL 4/192 ≈ 2.1%, which is below the 5% lower bound of the spec's null_share target for tags.id.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure the NULL share for tags.id (and other nullable FK columns) is at least 5% as the spec requires. The current child_null_share=0.15 default is applied before `_apply_null_rule`, but `_apply_null_rule` skips PK columns, so tags.id's NULL share is determined solely by child_null_share and the random draw; the observed 2.1% is below the 5% floor. Either raise child_null_share or apply the null_in_count_column window to nullable FK columns as well.

issues.evidence: The spec's null_targets list includes torrents.groupId, but the atomic summary shows torrents.groupId only has an unmatched_join_rows pattern (JOIN(tags.id=torrents.groupid)), not a null_in_count_column pattern. The program's `_null_shares` assigns a default 5-20% share to all nullable non-PK columns, so groupId gets NULLs, which is consistent with the null_targets list. This is a minor inconsistency between the atomic summary and the spec's null_targets, not a blocking error.
issues.requested_revision: No change required; note for the designer that the atomic summary omits a null_in_count_column pattern for torrents.groupId while the spec's null_targets includes it. The program's behavior (NULLs in groupId) is consistent with the spec.

unresolved_checks: The construction_pairs feedback shows 24 of 85 eligible pairs separated, with 0 unknown executions. This is a low separation rate but does not by itself prove a generation error; the spec's targets (like_near_variant, comparison_boundary, duplicates_for_distinct) are implemented in values.py and instance.py, and the low separation may reflect query-level equivalence rather than missing value variation. No held-out pairs were used.

The spec's uncertainty note says the groupYear upper bound 2015 is inferred, not observed. The program's column_bounds pads by ±2, producing values up to 2017, which may or may not be acceptable depending on the true domain. This is flagged as an issue above but the true domain is unknown.

The spec's releaseType enum lists 8 of 15 distinct values; the remaining 7 are unknown. The program does not enforce the enum, so generated values may include unknown-but-valid release types. This is flagged as an issue above.
